figures.subject: FIGURE BENEATH THE CORD

source.brief_excerpt: Floor-of-hands figure beneath red cord; top mounting point remains empty.

foras.name: FORAS
foras.appearance: He appeareth with six hands, five occupied in proving that the sixth is idle. His eyes are bare. He can see the failed part from his chair.
foras.powers: He knoweth the correction and the sound the machine made before it failed. He may describe either. He may perform neither until a superior hath approved the description. His one legion consisteth of himself and the person he is training to replace him; only one may be paid at a time.
foras.binding: A ticket number, a recorded greeting, and adherence to the current runbook, including its obsolete steps.
foras.seal: A small ring inside two larger rings: knowledge enclosed by permission.
foras.actual_effect: Located the fault in four minutes; left it running while permission was sought.
journey: The ticket entered with a wet corner. Water was coming through the ceiling of the place it described. Foras put a finger on a line in the drawing. Here, he said. Four minutes had elapsed.

The ticket asked him to turn the valve. He showed it the valve, the tool, and the paragraph that forbade him to use the tool on a valve already identified as faulty. An unidentified valve could be tested.

Could they unidentify it? That would require a correction to the record. The correction required the approval they were already waiting for. Foras sent the ticket downstairs, where people had more authority. He kept his finger on the line.
foras.parable: The repairer was asked to write down everything she knew. At the bottom she wrote: sometimes the noise matters. The editor removed this sentence because no noise had been specified.
